4.
After hearing both sides, I am of the considered opinion that the petitioners can be allowed to file a discharge petition before the trial court, if charge is not framed.
If such a discharge petition is filed, there can be a direction to consider the same, without insisting the presence of the petitioners.
While deciding the matter, the learned Magistrate will also consider the dictum laid down by the Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar's case (supra).

Therefore, this Criminal Miscellaneous Case is disposed of in the following manner:
1. The petitioners are free to file a discharge petition before the jurisdictional court within thirty days from the date of receipt of a stamped certified copy of this order, if charge is not framed.

2. Once such a discharge petition is received, the jurisdictional court will consider the same and pass appropriate orders in it, after giving an opportunity of hearing to the 2024:KER:72511 CRL.MC NO. 760 OF 2018 petitioners and the Prosecutor concerned, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of the discharge petition.

3. If a discharge petition is filed as directed above, the presence of the petitioners shall not be insisted, till final orders are passed in the discharge petition.
4.

While deciding the matter, the learned Magistrate will also consider the dictum laid down by the Apex Court in Kahkashan Kausar and Others v. State of Bihar and Others [AIR 2022 SC 820].
5. All the contentions raised by the petitioners in this criminal miscellaneous case are left open and the petitioners are free to agitate the same in the discharge petition.
